_comment: Tier-2 NUMERICAL GATE. EXERCISES THE NUMPY/SCIPY PATH, NOT KRATOS — the heat_transient catalog template declares 'Kratos (manual assembly)'. Pitfall (kratos.heat_transient #3): 'Consistent mass matrix gives better accuracy than lumped'. NOTE ON THE WRITTEN SIGNAL: this claim carries one of the five shared boilerplate Signal suffixes used across the Kratos catalog, which does not describe what actually happens. The real signal is recorded below and in the fixture output. Checked on the template's own consistent element mass (rho_cp*area/12*(ones+eye), which the template assembles) against its row-sum lumping: the two are shown to genuinely differ (consistent has non-zero off-diagonals, lumped is exactly diagonal) and to conserve the same total capacity (row sums match), and then the consistent matrix is measured to be the more accurate of the two against a well-resolved reference. Checking that the two matrices differ AND agree on row sums is what stops this being a comparison of a matrix with itself, or with a wrong one. All numbers asserted are the fixture's own output. Executed on Kratos 10.4.3 (pip wheels, glibc-2.31 host, fresh venv on external ext4 image).  INDEX RENUMBERED 3 -> 2: guidance entries were moved out of kratos.heat_transient's pitfalls list, which shifted the indices of the entries after them. The claim this fixture verifies is unchanged.
